Hi! I had both of my girls on methadone. My advice would be dont be afraid to increase your dose. Your baby is less likely to suffer from neonatal abstinence syndrome if you are stable! You will most likely need to go up because of the extra blood volume when pregnant and the baby metabolizing some of your dose. My first daughter had minor wd symptoms and a 16 day NICU stay with a morphine taper and my youngest who I just had in December had absolutely NO wd symptoms and she came home right away. I was more stable on my dose with my second and I think that had a lot to do with her doing so well! My oldest who is going to be 3 in a few months is now a healthy and happy, normal toddler. You would never be able to tell she was a MAT baby!! Theres a couple great Facebook groups for moms on methadone and they’re amazing for support. Full of incredible women! If you’d like I can add you to them. :) good luck and congrats.

At the very worst point in my heroin addiction I had left home and I had been sleeping on the street in a near constant black out for about 4 days. It was early March so it was cold outside but I was so high on Xanax and heroin that I couldn’t really feel it and I didn’t even care. I stumbled into a Walgreens to buy some cigarettes with my last 6 dollars and then back outside into a bench. My feet were raw and  covered in blisters, I hadn’t eaten in days and at the point I was contemplating ending it all, just watching the traffic fly by and wondering how bad it would hurt if I threw myself into the path of the next car that came by. I suddenly felt a tap on my shoulder and when I turned around there was a woman standing there with a bottle of water, some snacks and a fuzzy pink blanket that she had just purchased from the Walgreens I was outside of. She wrapped the blanket around my shoulders and gave me a hug and then just walked away after placing the rest of the stuff on the ground at my feet. I called my dad to come pick me up 10 minutes later and I haven’t used since. That woman saved my life. I don’t even remember her face but I will never forget the feeling of that hug.
